text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Talks on Pacific salmon collapse: 'Angry and surprised' Canadian envoy walks out as U.S. negotiators refuse to discuss catch reductions.
- Library ordered to pull bestseller: Winnipeg police mull porn charge.
- Chretien targets Charest on gun control: Liberals contend Tory leader is out of touch with Quebecers on key issue.
- National unity returns as passionate issue: The campaign was supposed to be about jobs, but it's about the age-old question.
- Children direct traffic in chaotic Kinshasa: While Kabila and top aides discuss 'reconstruction phase' of their revolution, capital is put on hold.
- Hudson's Bay eyes K mart: Plans bid for 36 stores; also may seek 10 Eaton's outlets for Zellers chain, president says.
- Tee-Comm's credit line put under review: DTH satellite TV operator pushed closer to brink as Bank of Montreal to re-examine debt facility.
- IBM stock sets record: Computer giant at US$175.12.
- CIBC, U.S. brokerage linked: Bank rumored to be looking at Oppenheimer.
- U.S. to abolish bank curbs: Bankers north and south fo the border brace for new era of competition as U.S. Treasury proposes to open access to lucrative securities and insurance markets.
